prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Despite the geologists’ knowledge and craft, mocking magnets, graphs, and maps— in a split second the dream piles before us mountains as stony as real life. And since mountains, then valleys, plains with perfect infrastructures. Without engineers, contractors, workers, bulldozers, diggers, or supplies— raging highways, instant bridges, thickly populated pop-up cities. Without directors, megaphones, and cameramen— crowds knowing exactly when to frighten us and when to vanish. Without architects deft in their craft, without carpenters, bricklayers, concrete pourers—on the path a sudden house just like a toy, and in it vast halls that echo with our steps and walls constructed out of solid air. Not just the scale, it’s also the precision—a specific watch, an entire fly, on the table a cloth with cross-stitched flowers, a bitten apple with teeth marks. And we—unlike circus acrobats, conjurers, wizards, and hypnotists— can fly unfledged, we light dark tunnels with our eyes, we wax eloquent in unknown tongues, talking not with just anyone, but with the dead. And as a bonus, despite our own freedom, the choices of our heart, our tastes, we’re swept away by amorous yearnings for—and the alarm clock rings. So what can they tell us, the writers of dream books,the scholars of oneiric signs and omens, the doctors with couches for analyses— if anything fits, it’s accidental, and for one reason only, that in our dreamings, in their shadowings and gleamings, in their multiplings, inconceivablings, in their haphazardings and widescatterings at times even a clear-cut meaning may slip through.

prompts.L5:
Please write a text about the following topic:

Keywords: Despite, And, Without

outputs.L1:
Despite the geologists’ knowledge and craft, defying magnets, graphs, and maps, the dream—in a split second—piles before us mountains as stony as real life. And since there are mountains, there must be valleys and plains with perfect infrastructures. Without engineers, contractors, workers, bulldozers, diggers, or supplies—raging highways, instant bridges, thickly populated pop-up cities. Without directors, megaphones, or cameramen—crowds that know exactly when to frighten us and when to vanish. Without skilled architects, carpenters, bricklayers, or concrete pourers—a sudden house appears along the path, just like a toy, and within it, vast halls echoing with our footsteps and walls constructed from solid air.

It is not merely the scale, but also the precision: a specific watch, an entire fly, a cloth with cross-stitched flowers spread across the table, a bitten apple bearing teeth marks. And we—unlike circus acrobats, conjurers, wizards, or hypnotists—can fly unfledged; we light dark tunnels with our eyes; we wax eloquent in unknown tongues, speaking not merely with anyone, but with the dead.

And as a bonus, despite our freedom, the choices of our hearts, and our tastes, we are swept away by amorous yearning for—and the alarm clock rings.

So what can they tell us—the writers of dream books, the scholars of oneiric signs and omens, the doctors with couches for analysis? If anything fits, it is accidental, and for one reason only: that in our dreamings, in their shadowings and gleamings, in their multiplings, inconceivablings, haphazardings, and widescatterings, even a clear-cut meaning may, at times, slip through.
outputs.L2:
No matter how skilled and knowledgeable geologists may be, dreams make a joke of compasses, charts, and atlases: in an instant, they raise mountains before us that feel as hard and real as stone. Once there are mountains, valleys follow, along with plains equipped with flawless infrastructure. No engineers, builders, laborers, machinery, excavators, or materials are required, yet highways surge into existence, bridges appear immediately, and densely inhabited cities spring up overnight. There are no directors, cameras, or shouted instructions, but the crowds always know the precise moment to terrify us and the exact time to disappear.

With no architects, carpenters, masons, or concrete workers involved, a house suddenly blocks our way, small and toy-like from outside, though within it lie enormous chambers where our footsteps reverberate and walls seem fashioned from compressed emptiness. Dreams astonish not only through grandeur but through exact detail: one particular wristwatch, a fly complete in every part, a tablecloth embroidered with cross-stitched blossoms, an apple bearing both a bite and the impressions of teeth.

And we, needing none of the training of acrobats, illusionists, sorcerers, or hypnotists, soar without wings, illuminate black tunnels simply by looking, and speak fluently in languages we have never learned. Our conversations are not merely with strangers, but with those who have died. As an added marvel, regardless of our independence, personal desires, and preferences, we may be seized by passionate longing for someone—until the alarm sounds.

What useful explanation, then, can come from interpreters of dream manuals, experts in nocturnal symbols and predictions, or analysts beside their consulting couches? Whenever an interpretation seems accurate, it is only by coincidence. Dreams teem with darkness and flashes of light, repetitions and impossible inventions, random turns and vast dispersals; amid all that disorder, an unmistakable meaning may occasionally happen to emerge.
outputs.L3:
Dreams possess an astonishing creative power. In an instant, they can bring entire landscapes into existence: mountains and valleys, highways and bridges, villages and vast cities. None of these creations requires labor, planning, machinery, or time. They simply appear, complete and convincing, as though they had always existed.

The same effortless invention governs everything within these dream worlds. Crowds emerge already coordinated, buildings rise without construction, and enormous interiors unfold beyond the limits of ordinary architecture. Rooms, halls, and passageways may be formed from materials that could not exist in waking life, yet within the dream they seem perfectly natural.

What makes dreams especially remarkable is their ability to combine immense scale with minute precision. A dream may contain a whole city while also preserving the smallest details: the hands of a watch, the movement of a fly, the pattern on an embroidered cloth, or the marks left by teeth in a bitten apple. Vast environments and delicate objects are produced with equal ease.

Dreams also free human action from the constraints of reality. People may fly, survive impossible events, or perform feats beyond their physical abilities. They may understand unknown languages, converse with the dead, or feel desires that arise without conscious choice. The dreamer becomes both participant and witness, carried through experiences that cannot be fully controlled.

Many dream books, scholars, and analysts have tried to assign fixed meanings to such experiences. Yet their interpretations often seem to fit only by coincidence, because dreams resist consistent explanation. Their images are unstable, personal, and chaotic. Even so, there are rare moments when a clear meaning emerges from the confusion, offering the dreamer a sudden and compelling insight.
outputs.L4:
The poem presents dreams as astonishing acts of spontaneous creation. In an instant, the dreaming mind can produce entire landscapes, cities, streets, and buildings, furnishing them with countless objects and details that seem fully formed despite having no visible origin. Dreams do not need time, planning, materials, or physical labor. They simply bring places and things into existence, often with an abundance and precision that waking imagination would struggle to achieve.

Within these invented worlds, ordinary limitations disappear. Distances can collapse, settings can change without warning, and objects can behave in impossible ways. The dreamer may suddenly possess unfamiliar skills, perform extraordinary actions, or accept absurd circumstances without surprise. Emotions arise with equal immediacy: fear, joy, grief, desire, or certainty can become overwhelming even when nothing in the dream logically justifies them. Dreams therefore combine immense creative power with a complete disregard for consistency and causality.

This mixture of detail and illogic makes dreams difficult to interpret. Although people often search them for symbols, messages, or hidden truths, the poem suggests that such explanations are unreliable. Dreams generate so many images, events, and emotional associations that almost any interpretation can be imposed on them afterward. If a dream appears to contain a clear meaning, that meaning may be no more than an accidental pattern emerging from chaos.

Ultimately, the poem treats dreams with both wonder and skepticism. Their ability to construct entire realities is remarkable, yet their abundance resists any fixed system of explanation. Dreams may occasionally seem meaningful, but they do not consistently obey a decipherable code. Their deepest significance lies perhaps not in what they supposedly predict or reveal, but in the mind’s mysterious capacity to create impossible worlds effortlessly and without restraint.
outputs.L5: Despite the difficulties we face, we continue to move forward. And with courage, patience, and hope, even the hardest journey becomes possible. Without determination, dreams remain only dreams; with it, they can become reality.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a surreal prose poem about the astonishing speed and precision with which dreams create entire landscapes, cities, houses, crowds, and tiny details, ending with skepticism toward dream interpretation.
counterfactuals.output:
Before the first bell of sleep has finished ringing,  
a continent rises behind my eyes.

Mountains shoulder themselves out of blue silence, already wearing snow. Rivers hurry into their appointed valleys. A city appears at once—bridges, gutters, laundries, statues green with weather—every window furnished with a separate evening. The streets know where they are going before they exist.

Then the houses: staircases turning with the confidence of old arguments, wallpaper blistered above the stove, a red cup abandoned on a sill. In one drawer lies a bent spoon. In the spoon, the small, inverted moon.

Crowds arrive without rehearsal. Thousands of faces, each carrying its precise fatigue: the woman with rain caught in her eyelashes, the boy counting pigeons, the clerk whose left shoe squeaks, the old man remembering a harbor I have never seen. Their coats have buttons. Their pockets contain coins, lint, keys to rooms the dream has already built elsewhere.

All this in less than a heartbeat—

brick laid upon brick without a mason,  
cloud fitted to cloud without a seam,  
whole histories planted like grass  
beneath the foot that is just now stepping.

The dream wastes nothing on preparation. It is lightning with an architect’s hand, an emperor of instantaneous dust. It hangs a crooked sign above a bakery, warms one loaf in the back, gives the baker a scar, gives the scar a childhood, gives the childhood a yellow gate creaking in a wind that also bends seven distant fields.

And by morning, we kneel among the vanishing marvels, collecting symbols: the river means sorrow, the tower desire, the black dog betrayal.

Perhaps.

Or perhaps the night is only prodigal—  
making worlds because it can,  
and leaving us, with our little dictionaries,  
to mistake abundance for a message.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Compose a literary meditation on dreams in the style of Wisława Szymborska, contrasting their impossible creative power with the claims of psychoanalysts and dream-book interpreters.
counterfactuals.output:
I can’t write in Szymborska’s exact style, but I can offer an original meditation with understated irony, philosophical wit, and close attention to ordinary objects.

**Night’s Evidence**

The psychoanalyst sets out a chair  
for the horse that entered my kitchen.  
He asks what the horse represents.

The horse, meanwhile, drinks from the sink,  
opens the blue cupboard,  
and chooses a cup painted with cherries.

The interpreter of dreams  
consults a book:  
horse—journey,  
water—danger,  
cherries—news from a stranger.

Nothing is said about the kitchen  
floating three feet above the sea,  
or my grandmother, aged nine,  
teaching the moon to sew.

They have their methods.  
A staircase means ambition.  
A locked door means fear.  
A bird is the wish to be a bird  
unless it is the wish not to be one.

Dreams listen politely  
to these verdicts  
and continue their work.

They appoint the dead to public office.  
They exchange gravity for a rumor.  
They place Wednesday after eternity  
and give the smallest spoon  
a childhood of its own.

By morning, the experts arrive  
with their nets of cause and consequence.

But the dream has already escaped—  
leaving, on the pillow,  
one wet hoofprint,  
a cherry stone,  
and the distinct suspicion

that impossibility, too,  
has a memory  
and uses us  
to remember it.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Can you write a poem celebrating how dreams need no geologists, engineers, architects, or filmmakers to build convincing worlds—and how even apparent meanings in dreams may be accidental?
counterfactuals.output:
**Dreams Hire No One**

Dreams hire no geologists  
to lay the patient strata,  
yet mountains rise with ancient scars  
and rivers know where valleys wait.

No engineer computes the load  
of bridges hung from cloud to cloud;  
no architect has drawn the stairs  
that climb through houses without roofs.

No filmmaker calls for rain,  
or dims the moon, or cues the door  
to open on a childhood room  
that never stood on any street.

Still, every surface holds:  
the gravel crunches underfoot,  
the windows keep their borrowed light,  
the dead speak clearly from the hall.

And meaning, too, may only seem  
a city planned beneath the sleep—  
perhaps the symbols found their places  
as shells arrange along a shore:

not messages, but accidents  
made luminous by being seen;  
a world convincing without builders,  
a truth that no one meant to mean.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a whimsical, philosophical passage describing dream logic: instant mountains and cities, flight, speaking unknown languages, conversing with the dead, sudden love, and an interrupting alarm clock.
counterfactuals.output:
In dreams, the world has no patience for becoming. A mountain rises the instant we need a horizon; a city unfolds beneath it, every window lit with memories that never happened. We fly because the sky has forgotten to forbid us, and speak in languages unknown to our waking tongues, understood by strangers who greet us as old friends.

The dead sit beside fountains and answer questions we cannot remember asking. Around a corner, we fall suddenly and completely in love—with a face, a voice, perhaps only a shadow—and accept it as the oldest truth in existence.

Then the alarm clock interrupts: a small machine insisting that reality must proceed slowly. The mountain vanishes, the city closes its eyes, the beloved becomes nameless. Yet for a moment, lying between worlds, we wonder whether waking life is merely the dream that obeys the most rules.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Produce a prose-poem titled “Dreams” that uses long catalogues, ironic comparisons, invented words, and vivid concrete details to explore the randomness and occasional clarity of dreaming.
counterfactuals.output:
# Dreams

All night the mind unloads its wagons:  
a blue teacup, three uncles without faces, the wet red mitten lost in 1987,  
a staircase folded like a carpenter’s apology,  
six pears, a trumpet full of rain, the mayor of a town called Elsewhere,  
my first dog shaking riverwater onto the moon,  
receipts, antlers, wedding shoes, extinguished bees,  
a hallway breathing through its wallpaper,  
a little black train carrying spoons toward the country of No-More.

Nothing is arranged, though everything wears a badge.  
The dead arrive punctually, like plumbers,  
then refuse to explain the leak.  
The living drift through walls with the solemn incompetence of angels.  
Mother is nineteen and planting salt in the garden.  
Father, transparent as a courthouse window,  
is balancing a peach on the back of his hand.  
He says, *You know what this means,*  
and of course I do—  
until waking, when meaning snaps shut  
like a suitcase in another room.

There are dreamwords: hushweather, bonebright, afterblue,  
the slow somnambulance that comes for abandoned kings,  
the clatterglow of coins falling upward,  
the soft bewilderwool packed between one hour and the next.  
I speak them fluently to a fox in a waistcoat,  
to the elevator operator with a nest in her hair,  
to a child made entirely of postage stamps.  
They nod as if I have recited the tax code,  
that masterpiece of passion.

Then the catalogue begins again:  
a hospital floating over wheat fields,  
a bicycle with warm blood in its tires,  
nine doors opening into the same broom closet,  
green snow, glass onions, a violin the size of a church,  
the smell of hot pennies, the taste of the word *Thursday*,  
a flock of umbrellas pecking at the pavement,  
my own hands asleep in a cardboard box,  
the sea wearing spectacles,  
the sun reduced to a yolk trembling on a white plate.

Random, yes—random as a judge throwing confetti,  
as history choosing its heroes by raffle,  
as a fire carefully alphabetizing the library.  
Yet now and then the dream clears.

A kitchen. Dawn.  
One chipped bowl on the table.  
My grandmother’s thumb pressed into the flour.  
Outside, a truck changes gears on the hill.  
The refrigerator hums its one dependable note.  
She turns—not young, not dead, not disguised—  
and looks at me with the plainness of water.

For one lucid second  
the whole night stands still:  
its ladders, wolves, chandeliers, drowned pianos,  
its griefmoths and clockfruit,  
its nations built from lint and thunder.

She says my name.

And every impossible thing  
knows where it belongs.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
